content: This medication is intended for your current condition only. Once your treatment is completed, dispose of any unused medication properly. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Different brands of this medication may have specific storage requirements. Refer to the product packaging for storage instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. To apply eye drops, first wash your hands thoroughly. Avoid wearing contact lenses while using this medication. Tilt your head back, look upward, and gently pull down the lower eyelid to create a small pouch. Hold the dropper directly above your eye and place one drop into the pouch. Look downward and gently close your eyes for 1 to 2 minutes. Apply gentle pressure to the inner corner of your eye (near the nose) with one finger to prevent the medication from draining out. Avoid blinking or rubbing your eye. Do not rinse the dropper after use. If you are using other eye medications (such as drops or ointments), wait at least 5 to 10 minutes before applying the next medication. Use this medication regularly at the same times each day to achieve the best results. Continue using it for the full duration prescribed, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Possible side effects include tearing, eye redness, eye discomfort, or eyelid itching/swelling. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to a new fungal eye infection. Do not use it for longer than prescribed. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not a complete list of side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using tobramycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other aminoglycosides (such as gentamicin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients (such as preservatives like benzalkonium chloride) that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. After applying this medication, your vision may become temporarily blurred or unstable. Use caution when performing activities that require clear vision. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Dispose of any unused medication after completing your treatment. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete and personalized medical advice.
